speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and when it started?

REQUEST TEST: Blood work for inflammatory markers and autoimmune panel.
REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the right wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal inflammatory and autoimmune results; since those are negative, can you tell me if you feel any clicking, locking, or grinding sounds in the wrist, and does the pain radiate into your fingers or thumb? REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the right wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome secondary to previous trauma.
